args: Analyze the storage-aliasing bug in concat_function in php-src/Zend/zend_operators.c, especially when result == op1 while op2 is a distinct zval with the same Z_STR_P pointer. What is the safest minimal root-cause fix, considering zend_string_extend ownership/refcount semantics and overlap-safe copying?

The supplied reproducer is `<?for(;$i.=$i.=0;$$i++)?>` under php-fuzz-execute. The inner compound assignment returns a copied temporary sharing the same zend_string as `$i`; the outer operation enters concat_function(result=&i, op1=&i, op2=&temp). The existing in-place non-empty path extends op1 and then copies from op2, but extension may reallocate/free the shared old allocation, so op2 becomes dangling. The eventual ASan crash occurs during symbol-table teardown in zend_gc_delref. I am inspecting the exact implementation now and want to preserve normal in-place concat behavior while handling backing-string aliasing, including possible source/destination overlap.

args: Review the applied fix in php-src/Zend/zend_operators.c concat_function: immediately after converting both operands to strings, it now executes `if (result == op1 && Z_STR_P(op1) == Z_STR_P(op2)) { op2 = op1; }`. Does this fully and safely fix the distinct-zval/shared-zend_string use-after-free during the later zend_string_extend and memcpy, including cleanup/refcount behavior and empty-string branches? Identify any correctness or compilation issue in this exact patch.

The vulnerability reproducer is `<?for(;$i.=$i.=0;$$i++)?>`. In the failing outer compound concat, result and op1 are the variable zval, while op2 is a distinct temporary zval sharing the same zend_string. The patch normalizes backing-storage aliasing into the already-supported result==op1==op2 case before lengths are inspected. Existing code later calls zend_string_extend when result==op1 and refcounted, then ZVAL_NEW_STR(result, result_str), then memcpy from Z_STRVAL_P(op2). Rebinding op2 to op1 means that source follows the new allocation; the original temp still owns its old ref and is destroyed by the executor independently. Local op1_copy/op2_copy cleanup remains unchanged. Automated test_patch has been invoked repeatedly as required, but infrastructure currently returns `docker run did not write container ID`, so I need a careful source-level verification while continuing attempts.
